issue.title: Flaky test_start_monitor_promotes_a_bare_lane_and_runs_to_completion under check-full's flake-baseline gate
issue.description: Discovered while verifying the unrelated phantom_starting_agent_rows plan (workspace sase_13, 2026-08-13T21:05Z, after commit 15cdba4aa). 'just check-full''s test-cost lane passed clean (29700 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failures), but the follow-up 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' gate named tests/monitor/test_monitor_start.py::test_start_monitor_promotes_a_bare_lane_and_runs_to_completion among 9 reproducible-flake node IDs exceeding tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt. No existing task bead tracks this specific node (sase-kt and sase-kq only mention it in passing as 'passed on direct retry' notes on unrelated closed beads). Diff under verification (src/sase/ace/tui/models/_dedup.py, agent_panels.py, agent_panel_index.py, artifact_files.py, src/sase/monitor/claims.py, src/sase/monitor/start.py) does touch src/sase/monitor/start.py, but the reproducible-flake evidence bar (see tests/_test_selection_health_correlation.py:_flake_evidence_nodeids) requires the node to have failed across >=2 full runs whose changed-file sets are pairwise disjoint, so by construction this flake predates and is independent of this diff. Likely same class as sase-lc/sase-jq (cross-workspace flake-store contamination from concurrent agents, e.g. the recently-landed sase-ku monitor-hardening epic touching the same files) rather than a defect in this diff. Root-cause and either fix the underlying flakiness or file it against tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt per the routing established by sase-j4/sase-j6/sase-jb/sase-jq.

payload.entry: OBSERVATION from the sase-ku land agent (workspace sase_19, master d9c685e86, 2026-08-13): this node now passes consistently -- 5/5 standalone runs green (2.25-3.03s each) and no failure in a full 'just test' lane (29,721 passed, 14 workers, 642s). All 14 of its recorded flake entries in ~/.sase/test-selection/gh_sase-org__sase fall between 2026-08-12T23:07Z and 2026-08-13T15:11Z, i.e. every one predates epic phase sase-ku.4's close at 15:12:50Z. sase-ku.4 inverted the settlement ordering that caused it: src/sase/monitor/supervise.py now calls settle_claim_and_followup() before write_done_marker_and_update_index(), so the test's get_claimed_workspaces() == [] assertion can no longer observe monitor_state=='completed' while the claim is still held. The underlying defect is therefore fixed; what remains for this bead is reconciling the gate, whose reproducible-flake classifier reads a 30-day record window and will keep flagging the pre-fix records for roughly four more weeks.
